outcomes.original: Filing step: Obtain a Certified Food Protection Manager certificate for at least one owner or employee, and ensure all food-handling employees complete the California Food Handler Card course within 30 days of hire. What to say: Register one owner or manager for an ANSI-accredited food safety certification exam (ServSafe, Prometric, NRFSP, or 360training) under California Health & Safety Code Section 113947.1; the course and proctored exam cost $100–$250 total, and the certificate is valid for five years. The certified manager must be on staff within 60 days of opening, and DPH asks for the certificate at the pre-opening inspection. Separately, every employee who handles food must obtain a California Food Handler Card from an ANSI-accredited provider ($7–$15, valid three years) within 30 days of hire. Keep both certificates on file for DPH inspections.

outcomes.original: Estimated time: 169 to 520 days. Estimated government cost: $5,523 to $21,970. Notes: The timeline is 169–520 days and the government cost is $5,523–$21,970 to obtain the three approvals in the entitlement path: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, estimated $3,100–$15,000), Health Permit to Operate (14–45 days, $470–$1,000), and Building Permit with change of use (14–120 days, $800–$15,000), plus San Francisco Business Registration ($55–$700), Public Health plan check ($828–$2,500), and prerequisite registrations (EIN free, California entity formation $70–$150, Seller's Permit free). The range represents the time to approval when the applications are granted. The CUA is the critical path: 4–10 months including pre-application meetings, environmental review, 300-foot mailed notice, posted notice, the Planning Commission hearing, and a 30-day appeal period. Building permit review (14–120 days) and Health permit processing (14–45 days) run in parallel or sequentially after the CUA is granted. The upper bound assumes the CUA takes the full 300 days, plan review encounters multiple correction cycles, and inspections are scheduled with delays; the lower bound assumes streamlined CUA processing (120 days), complete plan sets accepted on first submission, and prompt inspection scheduling. The cost range reflects construction-valuation-based fees for the building permit ($800–$15,000) and CUA fees that scale with project cost; a no-construction CUA is about $3,150 (2023–24 schedule, CPI-adjusted annually) but tenant improvements may increase the fee. Not included: construction costs, architect and contractor fees, workers' compensation insurance premiums (a percentage of payroll, not a government fee), ASCAP/BMI music licenses ($300–$2,500 each annually, private fees), sign permit ($300–$1,500), and expeditor or consultant fees. The timeline assumes applications are filed in the order given in the playbook and that the CUA is filed early, ideally before or during lease negotiation with a contingency clause, because it is the longest approval.
